title: How can you draw rotated squares and rectangles on a dot grid?
description: Two rotated squares and one rotated rectangle are drawn with their corners on dots, each by choosing steps across and up or down. The video then checks every figure with a ruler and the corner of a book.
teaching_notes: One idea: choose a step, turn it through a quarter turn for the next side, and the counts decide whether the figure is a square or a rectangle. Watch for children who draw a tilted figure by eye and never check its sides and angles.

source: Draw at least 3 rotated squares and rectangles on a dot grid. Draw them such that their corners are on the dots. Verify if the squares and rectangles that you have drawn satisfy their respective properties.
video_script.why: The child uses dot counts, as in the example in the book, to draw rotated squares and rectangles and then checks their sides and angles.
video_script.substitution: A diamond square with corners 4 dots up, right, down and left of its centre, a square with steps 3 across and 1 up, and a rectangle with steps 2 across 2 up and 3 across 3 up.
video_script.anchor: A dot grid with room for tilted squares and rectangles whose corners are on dots
video_script.payoff_line: Each figure drawn from dot counts passes the test for its shape.

final_answer.value: open ended; for example a diamond with corners 4 dots up, 4 dots right, 4 dots down and 4 dots left of its centre is a square, with 4 equal sides and 4 angles of 90 degrees
final_answer.spoken: each figure drawn from dot counts passes the test for its shape; for example a diamond with corners four dots up, four dots right, four dots down and four dots left of its centre is a square

never_show: the finished figures before the answer
maths_rules: Square 1: centre O, corners 4 dots up, 4 right, 4 down and 4 left of O. Each side goes 4 across and 4 down or up, so the 4 sides are equal; the sides turn through a quarter turn, so each angle is 90 degrees.

Square 2: P at (0, 0), Q at (3, 1), R at (2, 4), S at (-1, 3). The steps are 3 right 1 up, 1 left 3 up, 3 left 1 down, 1 right 3 down. Every side uses the counts 3 and 1, and each step is the previous one turned a quarter turn, so it is a square.

Rectangle: P at (0, 0), Q at (2, 2), R at (-1, 5), S at (-3, 3). The steps are 2 right 2 up, 3 left 3 up, 2 left 2 down, 3 right 3 down. Opposite sides use the same counts, so they are equal; the two kinds of step point along the two diagonals of the grid squares, at 90 degrees; the sides are not all equal, so it is a rectangle and not a square.
Check with a ruler for the sides and the corner of a book for the angles.
video_script.design: One idea: choose a step, turn it a quarter turn for the next side, and check. Uses dot counts from the example in the book. The dot grid stays all video.
open_questions: The three figures are chosen here; the book leaves the drawing to the child.
